text:
On looking at my cheeks, red only yesterday,

I have felt autumn; its old age's ailments

have filled me with fear; the mirror has told me

that it snows in my hair while the leaves fall…


What a curious fate! It has knocked at my doors

in the full springtime to offer me snow,

and my hands grow icy beneath the light pressure

of a hundred blue roses dead upon their fingers.


I already feel myself wholly invaded by ice;

my teeth chatter while the sun outside

sets patches of gold, as in spring,

and laughs in the sky's unfathomable depth.


And I weep slowly, with a cursed pain…

with a pain that weighs upon all my fibers,

O pale death that offers me a wedding

and the blurred mystery laden with infinity!


But I rebel!… How can this human form,

which cost matter so many transformations,

kill, inside my breast, all my illusions

and bring me night at almost full morning?

translation.title: On Looking at My Cheeks, Red Only Yesterday...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet-like quatrain structure and the poem's reversal of spring into premature winter. The source reads “enson[d]ada” (apparently a typo for “insondada,” unfathomable); the English uses “unfathomable” while noting the source irregularity here.
